A muscle fibre relaxes when its motor neuron stops firing, so acetylcholine is cleared from the neuromuscular junction and no new action potentials are generated. SERCA then actively pumps Ca²⁺ back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and tropomyosin re-blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin. The question is cut off after "when:", so this assumes the standard textbook answer, and confidence is lower than before for that reason.

CONFIDENCE: 60
